name: [Portal] First entry of an existing partner: account linking and onboarding
description:
### Summary

Most partners who will use the Partner Portal already exist: API partners with an approved partner record in the legacy API database, and agencies or freelancers who administer client shops with a Shoptet admin account. This task covers what happens the first time such a person logs into the portal with their existing Shoptet credentials. The portal has to recognise which partner record the user belongs to, show the partner profile that was migrated from the public partner websites so the user can review it, take the user through the terms acceptance flow, and then land them on the overview with only the sections that make sense for their partner type. The task also handles the awkward cases: a user with no partner record yet, a user who administers several shops, and a partner record that has no admin user attached. Self-registration and inviting colleagues are separate tasks. Depends on the partner mapping, the profile import, the login screen, the shell and the terms acceptance task.

### Why?

The MVP opens in April 2027 to existing partners first, so the very first session of a long-standing agency or API partner decides whether the portal feels like a continuation of their relationship with Shoptet or like a stranger asking them to start over. Their data already lives in the legacy API partner table, in project user synchronisation and, after the import, in the CRM partner record, but nothing links a logging-in person to those records yet. Getting the link wrong would expose one partner's profile to another or leave a partner without access, so this step needs explicit rules and edge-case handling. It is also the natural moment for the terms acceptance and the review of the migrated profile.

### What?

An existing partner signs in with the Shoptet admin credentials they already use and, without any manual step by Shoptet staff, is recognised as a member of the right partner record and led through a short first-entry sequence: terms acceptance, a review of the migrated profile with a clear way to correct it later, and arrival on the overview showing only the sections for their partner type. A user with no partner record is told so and offered to create a profile. A user administering several shops chooses which partner they act for, or asks to merge duplicates. A partner record without any admin user can be claimed through e-mail verification against the record's contact address. Every later login skips the sequence and goes straight to the overview.

### Acceptance Criteria

A user whose admin account is linked to a project with an approved legacy API partner record, or to a CRM partner record, logs in with existing credentials and is attached to that partner without staff action; the link is persisted and reused on later logins.

On first entry the user passes the terms acceptance flow, then sees the migrated profile with a visible path to the edit screen, then the overview; on second and later logins none of these steps repeat.

Overview sections are enabled per partner type (API partner, agency/freelancer, affiliate) and disabled sections are not reachable by URL.

A user with no matching partner record sees an explanation and an offer to create a profile; no partner record is created silently.

A user linked to several projects with distinct partner records is asked to choose the partner to act for and can flag duplicates for merge; the choice is remembered.

A partner record without an admin user can be claimed only after a verification e-mail to the record's stored contact address is confirmed; the e-mail exists in cs, sk, hu and en.

Every automatic link and every claim is logged with user, partner and reason so Partnership can audit it in CRM.

New PHP passes PHPStan level 10 (

make phpstan-l10

) with unit tests for the matching rules; the React screens pass 

make fe-test

 and 

make lint

.

### Open questions

- Wiki Q7: what the first entry of an existing partner must contain beyond terms and profile review (e.g. confirming contact e-mails, choosing portal language).
- Which partner types get access in the first MVP wave — all at once, or API partners first with agencies following once import quality is verified.
- How the `partnerPortal` module is enabled for existing partners: per project (flag on the partner's own project) or per partner record in CRM, and who switches it on.
- Matching precedence when signals disagree (legacy API partner status, isPartner flag in project user sync, CRM partner e-mails) — DevRel decides during implementation per wiki Q4.
- Whether a public vs. billing e-mail mismatch blocks the claim flow or only warns.

### Technical notes

_Generated by Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-09-16_

- Module gate: `admin/controllers/PartnerPortal/PartnerPortalOverviewController.php` uses `#[RequiresActiveModule('partnerPortal')]`; React pages under `admin/react/src/PartnerPortal/pages/`. Enabling the module per existing partner project is an operational question (see Open questions).
- Legacy API partner: `st_api.partner` (`status` enum pending/approved/suspended/rejected, `projectId`, `userId`, `homepage`) and `cms/packages/Connectors/Model/ApiPartner.php` (`STATUS_APPROVED` etc.).
- Per-project users: `project_users_synchronization` in `database/schema/st_cms.sql` (`adminUserId`, `email`, `role` enum user/partner/manager/owner, `isPartner`, `isOwner`, `loginCount`, `lastLogin`), synced by `cms/packages/Synchronization/Users/ProjectUsersSync.php` — basis for the several-projects case.
- CRM partner master: `st_crm.partner` (`projectId` nullable, `emailForCommunication`, `emailForSync`, `status`) and `partner_lng`; the user → partner mapping itself is delivered by , the imported profiles by .
- Login helpers: `cms/packages/Profiles/Helper/AdminUserHelper.php` (`getCrmAdminUserByCredentials` ~L300, `createAndSaveRenewHashCrm` ~L864).
- Claim e-mail via the `ActionEmailBuilder` pattern (`cms/packages/Email/ActionEmailBuilder.php`), templates cs/sk/hu/en. Link and audit tables go to `database/schema/st_crm.sql` via `migrations/2026/devrel/crm/` (`migrations/AGENTS.md`).
